posts.topic_title: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.author: tpark
posts.post_subject: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.content_md:
Hi,

Last Thursday I was over at a friends place making some reflection holograms, and we have encountered a rather strange problem with the produced holograms. A reflection hologram was made with a coin about 3mm from the plate worked fine, but one where the coin was 1mm from the plate appeared to have no image, but an image could be seen with the white light replay beam at a very steep angle, almost perpendicular to the plate. The beam came from a 60mw 654nm diode laser, with the beam at a 45 degree angle to the plate. 1.5 mj/cm^2, 2 1/2 inch square PFG03M plates developed with JD4. Density looked OK when developed. I think it's possible that the reflection off the coin was too strong, causing problems but I'm not sure. Has anyone else encountered something like this? We tried a couple of plates with this jig and the coin up close, and each time we get similar results. 

Thanks,

--Ted.

posts.topic_title: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.author: edelbrp
posts.post_subject: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.content_md:
> **tpark:** I think it's possible that the reflection off the coin was too strong, causing problems but I'm not sure. Has anyone else encountered something like this?

I doubt that the reflection is too strong. I'd suspect movement as the culprit. Are you settling for a long time (at least 10 min)? Is the temp of the coin(s) the same as the plate (and same as the environment)? I've done lots of Denisyuks with the plate set directly onto some very shiney coins, and haven't had this kind of problem. I've had lot of issues that I'd attribute to movement, though. I try to make two holograms during a session. The first tends to come out, and the second tends not to. I'm pretty certain that my failures on the second are due to my lack of patience or over fiddling.

BTW- 60mw is a lot of power for such a small plate. That's a fraction of a second exposure, isn't it?

-Phil

We tried a couple of plates with this jig and the coin up close, and each time we get similar results.

I have seen that odd angle image effect, it can be caused by the coin's 

image acting as a (usually convex mirror in parts) so that you can get a strong transmission hologram as the coin sends 2 beams back from one side. This can then back reflect from the plate/air interface on the side opposite the coin to give a peculiar angled reflection hologram again with coin acting as its own reference beam. Did you get a strong transmission one too? Anyway , it would seem you may have spoilt your primary reflection one by over exposure so that there were no silver halide grains left unexposed along the plane your primary exposure angle . -- But this is just a guess, I could be wrong.

posts.author: olegg555
posts.post_subject: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.content_md:
Actually, PFG-03M was never ment to be used with JD-4 and bleaching. 

It's emulsion and grain structure are designed for physical development such as GP2 or GP3 process. I tried JD4 a few times: holograms are hard to see. Another thing is high-power laser diodes: they tend to heat up and this affects quality of the emitted beam. 

Regards,

Oleg.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.post_subject: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.content_md:
This is just a different thought direction. Whenever coin is stated as the object I think about polarization. If the differences in distances were greater I would think this could be the culprit. But from 1mm to 3 mm is such a small amount of difference, this thinking is deterred.

Is the coin very shiney throughout? Or is it very used and dull? The first would produce shiney polarization dependent reflections. The latter would produce two kinds of reflections. Diffuse and non diffuse (polarization and non polarization dependent) reflections. To elliminate polarization effects, is it possible to paint the coin flat white? Was the emulsion facing the coin or away from the coin. This would change the actual distance from coin to emulsion which may allow the non diffuse reflections to miss the center of the plate while the diffuse reflection would hit the center of the plate. Was the laser rotated in any way from the 3mm to the 1mm set up? 

Photos would be great to see!

Yes Michael.

I am sure that Jd4 is not a propper developer for PFG03.

Main reason why JD4 used is less toxic chemistry (what is very important for class rooms with children) and faster developing time. Bleaching will dissolve a lot of fine graines of silver (that is why PFG03 has low sensitivity) and loss of diffraction efficiency will take place. 

Oleg.

Bleaching will dissolve a lot of fine graines of silver (that is why PFG03 has low sensitivity) and loss of diffraction efficiency will take place.Oleg.

There seems to be some discrepancy with regards to PFG-03: one "philosophy" stresses on the importance of colloidal (solution-physical) development - the other one on chemical development and rehalogenating bleaching.

I have used hydroquinone/metol developers (similar to VRP), followed by PBU-Metol or copper sulfate bleaches with good results.

Maybe the whole thing boils down to differences from one batch to another.

posts.author: tpark
posts.post_subject: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.content_md:
Thanks for all the replies.

I suppose that settling time could be an issue, I'll try letting it settle longer. Also, the exposure time seems a bit suspect - I measured the power levels, and all seemed fine, plus the density of the plate seemed OK as well. The total energy of the laser is not on the plate, thus the longer exposure time.

I've used PFG-03M with JD-4 extensively, and I've generally had very good results. 

The coin I used was a fairly new gold coin. Another pass used a silver coin, also in good shape.

I think next exposure I will use much less light. I've had good results with this laser on other exposures (even in the same session), but I think there's something odd going on with the geometry/exposure with this particular setup.

The emulsion was facing the plate BTW.

JohnFP: The laser was not rotated from exposure to exposure - I used an optima LDM 1100 mount, and that's bolted onto the frame. I will take some photographs the next time I'm over there with my digital camera.

Jeff-blyth: It seems as though that's a distinct possibility, as now we have 3 odd angle replay holograms. 

Olegg555: It is possible that this is an issue, as before I was using a diode set to 18mw of output, and another with 25. The diode is in a mount that acts as a good heat sink, and I give it lots of time to stabilize. This device hasn't produced any "banded" holograms, except for one TEA soaked BB640 plate, but that exposure is a bit suspect as both impatience and beer figured into the production of that hologram.

Thanks again for you replies - I'll keep you posted on how the next session goes.

--Ted

posts.topic_title: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.author: Dinesh
posts.post_subject: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.content_md:
The effect you're seeing is due to the specular reflection of the coin and beam ratios. It's got nothing to do with polarisation.

The light goes through the plate at 45 degrees. The incoming light illuminates the entire plate but reflects off the coin at 45 degrees the other way. The return beam from the coin therefore mostly misses the incoming reference, except at 45 degrees below the plate (and presumably coin) normal. That is it meets the reference beam that exists at 45 degrees below the coin. At normal incidence, there's very little reflectivity from the coin back to the plate and so the ratio is practiaclly non-existant. To overcome this, paint the coin a flat white so there's Lambertain reflection. If the coin were at some angle, the reflectivity of the edges would also hit the plate at a lower angle more intensely and increase the "local" beam ratio.

Transmission-Reflection-Transmission. Pretty ingenious, Jeff! However, wouldn't the two components from either egde of the coin reflect away from the viewer at the second reflection (back of plate/air - front of plate). But, I assume you're familiar with the fact that a reflection hologram can be seen in transmssion? I use this effect to check my processing of reflection holograms.The brighter the transmission (achromat) image, the better is going to be my reflection.

However, they produce slightly less bright holograms.Oleg.

That authorship indeed is ridiculous.

I guess one important difference between colloidal developed layers and

chemically developed/rehalogenating bleached refers to bandwidth. I am aware

of very large bandwidths with some GP type developed emulsions.

A serious issue with colloidal developed layers may be their intrinsic

absorption though. That seems to relate to the size/shape of the metal silver

"discs". I understand it becomes difficult to develop a layer having

little absorption at short wavelengths. In my view FMG-1 (or the very

diluted developer I used, "Collo-1") produced significantly smaller grains than 

GP-2 etc. Hence it was possible to preswell the emulsion in

TEA and yet achieve bright green reconstructions.

I wonder about the limits of colloidal development, particularly if it's

possible to produce layers with weak blue light absorption...

posts.topic_title: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.author: tpark
posts.post_subject: Problems with making a reflection hologram on PFG-03M
posts.content_md:
Well, we looked at the holograms again, and it appears as though the intense reflection off the coin was the problem. The mounting has a black background, and if the hologram is illuminated as it should be for replay, a careful viewing of the hologram shows the background as a dim red area, and a big black hole where the coin is. The laser we were using showed some mode hopping problems on some deeper holograms, when the 20mw laser (which had been tuned up to be in a non mode hopping zone) we got several good holograms off the jig. 

Thanks again for your help.

--Ted
